Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

spatialkit 3.0.0

This release follows 2.0.0, published on CRAN on 2026-09-11. It adds a choice of the number of cells from the data (resolution_profile(), select_resolution()), pooled cell values with intervals as the default of summarize_by_cell(), density-weighted seeds as the default partition, and a GWR the package solves itself, without GWmodel. Read Breaking changes before upgrading a running analysis.

Breaking changes

Defaults that change results

  • summarize_by_cell() adds pooled values by default (estimate = "pooled"). Beside each mean it returns ..pooled_*, ..pooled_w_* and ..pooled_target_* for every numeric response and predictor, and the attributes "pooled" and "intervals". Every column 2.0.0 returned is unchanged. The default call can now raise the warnings of the pooled values (spatialkit_pool_unavailable, spatialkit_pool_degenerate, spatialkit_pool_few_cells, spatialkit_no_structure and others), and small or unstructured layers raise several. estimate = "mean" leaves the pooled columns and their attributes out.

  • get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans") and voronoi_seeds_kmeans() build density-weighted seeds by default (partition = "density"). Each point is weighted by its local density, so cells are small where observations are dense and hold about the same number of observations each once there are more cells than dense places. The seeds are the best of 3 k-means++ starts (kmeans_nstart = NULL, nstart = NULL). Every default call returns other seeds and other cells. partition = "kmeans" restores stats::kmeans() from 10 random starts; on gridded locations its seeds can still differ, because the coordinates are now centred and scaled before clustering.

  • voronoi_seeds_random() draws from the session’s random stream by default (set_seed = NULL). The 2.0.0 default, 456, returned the same seeding on every call, even inside a loop over set.seed(). set_seed = 456 restores the 2.0.0 seeds.

  • area_of_applicability() weights the predictors by the model’s variable importance by default (weights = "auto"). It uses pmax(importance, 0) when the model carries a finite importance for every predictor and has out-of-bag skill, and equal weights otherwise; params$weights_source says which. weights = NULL restores the equal weights of 2.0.0.

  • area_of_applicability() measures location for models that predict from it. A GWR fit, a Bayesian GP fit and a random forest fitted with include_coords = TRUE get a location index (DI_location), and a point is inside only when it is inside on both indices. The location index refuses a train_sf in a geographic CRS; project it or pass coords = "no". For a forest, a row outside on location is FALSE where a missing predictor made it NA. coords = "no" restores the 2.0.0 result for a GWR or Bayesian fit; for a forest it leaves the coordinates out of both indices.

  • fit_rf_model() splits an unordered factor or character predictor with respect.unordered.factors = "order". ranger’s default, "ignore", splits on the order in which the levels are stored, so forests with such a predictor change. $info$respect_unordered_factors records the setting and print() shows it. Passing respect.unordered.factors = "ignore" through ... restores the 2.0.0 forest.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() samples with adapt_delta = 0.99 by default, up from 0.9. cv_bayes(), compare_models_cv() and any other call that leaves control unset do the same. At 0.9 ordinary layers left a few divergent transitions, and a single one sets convergence_ok to FALSE. Sampling takes longer, and a fit at a given seed draws different values. control = list(adapt_delta = 0.9) restores the 2.0.0 setting.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model(standardize_predictors = TRUE) scales its automatic slope prior to the response. The prior is normal(0, 2.5 * sd(y)) under an identity link and normal(0, 2.5 * sd(log(y))) for the lognormal families; other links keep normal(0, 5), the 2.0.0 prior for every family. On a response in dollars the fixed prior shrank a real slope to almost nothing. $info$b_prior records the prior used. Passing prior = brms::set_prior("normal(0, 5)", class = "b") restores the 2.0.0 prior.

  • select_features_forward() accepts a candidate by the rule rule = "se". Its pooled gain must exceed tol and the mean of its per-fold gains must exceed se_mult (default 1) standard errors of that mean. With the 2.0.0 default, tol = 0, any gain was accepted, so the selections change. rule = "tol" restores the 2.0.0 test.

  • determine_optimal_levels() returns NA where its WSS curve has no elbow (on_no_elbow = "na"). The count it returned there was where the chord rule lands on a curve with no bend, about the square root of max_levels whatever the points. A layer of one or two points, or of one location, also gives NA, where it gave 1. A warning of class spatialkit_no_elbow carries the count. on_no_elbow = "warn" returns the count with that warning.

  • estimate_sac_range() bins the variogram at adaptive lags (lags = "adaptive"). The first bin ends where the closest max(50, n / 4) pairs lie and the rest widen geometrically to the cutoff. The 2.0.0 fifteen equal bins hid structure shorter than the first bin. Ranges, nuggets and the block sizes of make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) change. lags = "equal" restores the 2.0.0 bins.

  • estimate_sac_range() tests for spatial structure before it returns a range (structure_alpha = 0.05). The test is Moran’s I of the modelled variable on its 2, 4, 8 and 16 nearest neighbours, Bonferroni-adjusted. When it finds none, the result is NA with the rejected_reason “no spatial structure detected at the nearest-neighbour scale”. structure_alpha = 1 switches the test off.

  • The GWR functions choose the default bandwidth by a search of their own. With bandwidth = NULL, fit_gwr_model(), gwr_model_selection() and cv_gwr() score 16 log-spaced bandwidths and refine the best, where GWmodel::bw.gwr()’s golden-section search returned a near-global bandwidth when AICc had two minima. When rows share a location, the search minimises the leave-one-location-out sum of squares, not AICc, with a warning of class spatialkit_gwr_repeated_locations. info$bandwidth_search keeps the scored curve. Supplying bandwidth fixes it; no argument reruns the 2.0.0 search.

  • plot_tessellation_map(labels = TRUE) reads the first ID column the layer has (label_col = NULL). The order is poly_id, polygon_id, id, cell_id and grid_id, the order in which assign_features_to_polygons() reads a polygon layer’s IDs. The 2.0.0 default read grid_id alone, which no layer the package builds carries, so it drew no labels. label_col = "grid_id" restores it.

Across the pipeline

  • FNN moves from Suggests to Imports. The nearest-neighbour searches use it, the one behind the density partition among them. The package’s exact searches remain for a session in which FNN cannot be loaded; they give the same results in a time that grows with the square of the number of locations.

Measure spatial autocorrelation

  • estimate_sac_range() fits its variogram model without iteration. For each trial range the nugget and partial sill are solved exactly under gstat’s criterion, so the same layer gives the same verdict, range and nugget in any unit and row order. Every range and nugget moves a little, only the exponential family is fitted, and the rejected_reason “variogram model did not converge” no longer occurs. No argument restores the 2.0.0 fit.

  • estimate_sac_range() never returns the largest directional range in place of an all-pairs fit. Where the all-pairs fit identifies no range, or its range runs past the largest lag fitted, the result is NA. The directional ranges are still attached, and anisotropy_used is always FALSE. No argument restores the 2.0.0 result.

  • estimate_sac_range() needs 30 distinct locations as well as 30 rows. Rows that share a location are one place to the variogram and to the test for structure. A layer of 30 or more rows at fewer distinct locations gets the unclassed NA whose rejected_reason gives the count. So summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram") falls back to Kish and make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) builds geometric blocks on such layers. No argument restores the 2.0.0 result.

  • estimate_sac_range() words one rejected_reason differently. Where fewer than three lag bins hold point pairs it reads “no variogram model could be fitted: fewer than three lag bins hold point pairs”, where 2.0.0 read “no variogram model could be fitted (singular fits)”. Both start “no variogram model could be fitted”, which a script can compare instead.

Choose a resolution

  • determine_optimal_levels() fits each count as the best of 25 k-means++ restarts, where 2.0.0 ran stats::kmeans(nstart = 5). Its WSS curve rose at one or two steps on clustered layouts, and the elbow rule could select such a bump. The elbow is now read on log-log axes and counts only where the curve sags clearly below a straight line. Counts can differ from 2.0.0’s, most on clustered layers. No argument restores the 2.0.0 sweep.

  • determine_optimal_levels() keeps the criterion it is given. Supplying both response_var and predictor_vars switched the default criterion = "geometric" to "combined", also when "geometric" was named. Such a call now returns what the call without the two variables returns. Naming criterion = "combined" takes the path of the switch; no argument restores its 2.0.0 ranking.

  • determine_optimal_levels(criterion = "combined") ranks the counts around the elbow by the log-log sag of the WSS curve alone. Moran’s z of the cell means stays in attr(, "diagnostics") but no longer ranks: its |z| is near 0 at the coarsest counts it scores whatever the response, so it put the lowest count first. With an elbow the elbow comes first; with none the order is that of "geometric". No argument restores the 2.0.0 ranking.

  • determine_optimal_levels(criterion = "morans_i") raises a warning of class spatialkit_diagnostic_ranking. It still ranks by Moran’s z of the cell means, which grows as cells get finer than the autocorrelation range and so favours fine counts whatever the data. The warning names resolution_profile() and select_resolution() as the alternative. The counts are unchanged.

Build the cells

  • build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") on seeds builds cells over the data the seeds stand for. Without a boundary, 2.0.0 clipped the cells to the seeds’ own hull, and the assignment dropped the observations outside it. The seeding functions now attach the boundary they drew in, or the hull of the points they clustered, as attr(, "cover"), and the cells are built over it. Passing boundary sets the extent; no argument restores the clip to the seeds’ hull.

  • get_voronoi_seeds() stops on a number of starts that is not whole, such as kmeans_nstart = 2.5, under the default density partition, with “kmeans_nstart must be NULL or a single positive whole number of starts”. With partition = "kmeans" the call returns as in 2.0.0.

Assign and summarise

  • assign_features_to_polygons() stops on a duplicated or missing value in the polygon ID column. In 2.0.0 nine polygons keyed by a zone attribute called id, which repeats, came back as three. When rows that share an ID are parts of one unit, merge them first, for example with dplyr::summarise(dplyr::group_by(polygons_sf, <ID column>)). No argument restores the 2.0.0 result.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram") falls back to "kish", not to the uncorrected standard error, when no usable variogram exists. A warning of class spatialkit_deff_fallback gives the reason, and a new column deff_method names the correction each row carries. A variogram refused for want of spatial structure gives a design effect of 1, with a warning of class spatialkit_deff_no_structure naming the predictor columns. deff = 1 gives the uncorrected standard errors.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "kish") estimates one ICC per predictor. 2.0.0 pooled one ICC over every predictor listed, so listing a second predictor changed the first one’s standard error. attr(, "icc")$pred and attr(, "deff_applied")$icc_pred are vectors named by predictor. No argument restores the pooled ICC.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "kish") returns NA standard errors for a column whose ICC cannot be estimated. That is a column with values in one cell only, or fewer than two cells holding two or more of its values. 2.0.0 returned the uncorrected standard errors under the corrected label. ..neff_*, ..ci_* and cell_weight are NA in those cells too, and a warning of class spatialkit_icc_unavailable names the columns. deff = 1 gives the uncorrected standard errors.

Fit a model

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() sets $info$convergence_ok by stricter checks. It is FALSE on any divergent transition, an R-hat above 1.05, an R-hat above 1.01 with fewer than 100 effective draws per chain, a bulk or tail effective sample size under 100 per chain, or an E-BFMI under 0.3. Short runs that passed in 2.0.0 can fail. One warning of class spatialkit_convergence names each failed check and its remedy. No argument restores the 2.0.0 checks.

  • fit_gwr_model() solves the local regressions itself, and GWmodel is no longer needed to fit, predict, cross-validate or select (sp still is). The solve is pivoted QR on predictors centred in each window. A coefficient a rank-deficient window cannot estimate is NA, with a warning of class spatialkit_gwr_rank_deficient, where 2.0.0 stopped the fit. On windows of full rank the results equal GWmodel::gwr.basic()’s to rounding. fit$engine is a list in GWmodel’s layout, not an object of class gwrm. No argument restores the 2.0.0 engine.

  • new_spatial_fit() stops on a fit its methods cannot use. The error names the argument: data_sf must be an sf object with a geometry column, response_var one attribute column, predictor_vars attribute columns other than the response, and formula must hold the response on its left and use the columns predictor_vars names on its right. A fit_fn that passed st_drop_geometry(train_sf) must pass train_sf; a column derived inside fit_fn must be added to train_sf or left out of predictor_vars. No argument restores the 2.0.0 checks.

Check a fit in sample

  • The metrics frames gain n_MAPE and n_SMAPE. model_metrics(), summary(), evaluate_insample(), compare_models() and the overall and fold_metrics of the cv_*() functions and compare_models_cv() carry the rows each percentage error was averaged over. The columns follow Adj_R2, so code that addresses the metric columns by position is unaffected; code that pins the exact column set needs the two names. cv_bayes()’s fold_metrics and compare_models() gain convergence_ok in the same way. No argument removes the new columns.

Cross-validate and compare

  • compare_models_cv() stops when it cannot build its shared fold set. In 2.0.0 it logged a line and fell back to each backend’s default blocks, so the comparison ran on folds the caller had not asked for. The error gives the reason. No argument restores the fallback.

Choose predictors

  • select_features_forward() gives every learner a baseline to beat. A forest or a GWR in 2.0.0 had none, so at least one variable was always selected. The baseline is now the learner’s own null model (a GWR fits one), the new null_fn, or the mean of each training fold, and the selection can be empty. No argument restores the 2.0.0 behaviour.

Set options, catch conditions and clear caches

  • prep_model_data(), assign_features_to_polygons() and make_folds() raise classed R warnings where they logged a line, so tryCatch(), withCallingHandlers() and options(warn = 2) see them. They cover rows dropped before a fit (spatialkit_rows_dropped), a constant predictor (spatialkit_constant_predictor), features in no polygon (spatialkit_unassigned) and fewer folds than asked for (spatialkit_k_reduced, with fields k_requested and k). ?"spatialkit-conditions" lists every class. No argument restores the log lines.

New features

New functions

  • resolution_profile() and select_resolution() choose the number of cells from the data. By default the profile scores one size, about 4.5 observations per cell (obs_per_cell = "auto"), for pooled cell values (estimate = "auto"). levels or n_levels give a ladder of counts instead, scored by Mallows’ Cp, the reliability of the cell means, the WSS elbow and the leave-one-out error. select_resolution() reads a count off the profile with its flat region, and summary() and plot() set the criteria side by side. get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans() and build_tessellation() take a profile or a selection as the count. See vignette("resolution").

  • cell_values_at() returns the value and interval of the cell at other locations, with each location’s distance from the nearest observation. See vignette("cells").

  • kriging_adequacy() computes, beside the plain means, what block kriging would give each cell from a fitted variogram: the kriged estimate and variance, the error variance of the plain mean under the same variogram (plain_var) and the share of it kriging removes (kr_gain), with a cross-validated check of the kriging variance. See vignette("cells").

  • sac_nugget() returns the nugget variance behind an estimate_sac_range() result. See vignette("spatial-cross-validation").

  • fold_separation() measures, for each fold, the distance from every held-out point to its nearest training point. Given prediction_points, it sets those distances beside the distances from the locations to be predicted to the data, and says whether the cross-validated error tends to read low or high for that map. See vignette("spatial-cross-validation").

  • cv_block_size_sweep() runs one cross-validation at a ladder of block sizes, with random folds as the reference, and returns the error at each size with its fold-to-fold spread and the estimated autocorrelation range; plot() draws the curve. A fit budget (max_fits) refuses a sweep that would run past it. See vignette("spatial-cross-validation").

  • plot_cv_metrics() draws one point per fold for a metric of a cv_*() or compare_models_cv() result, sized by the held-out rows, with the pooled value as a dashed line. plot_calibration() draws the observed against the nominal coverage of cv_bayes()’s predictive intervals, pooled and per fold. See vignette("spatial-cross-validation").

Prepare the data

  • ensure_projected() gains purpose = c("distance", "area"). "area" chooses among equal-area projections, for densities or rates per cell. The CRS chosen for lon/lat input comes with attr(, "crs_choice"), the candidates and each one’s measured distance error, and projected input has its area distortion measured and logged as a warning above 1 percent.

  • prep_model_data() records the rows it drops in attr(x, "dropped") (n, which, row_id, reason). Every fit carries the count as $info$n_dropped, and every cv_*() result as n_dropped. The prepared layer has the class "spatialkit_rows" after "sf"; [ and the dplyr row verbs return it without the record.

Measure spatial autocorrelation

  • estimate_sac_range() gains detrend = c("ols", "reml") and reml_max_n. A variogram of least-squares residuals underestimates the range (Lark, Cullis and Welham 2006). "reml" fits the trend and an exponential-plus-nugget covariance together with nlme::gls(), on at most reml_max_n points. The default "ols" detrends as 2.0.0 did. nlme joins Suggests.

  • estimate_sac_range() reads rows that share a location as one place: the test for structure uses the location means, pairs at zero separation enter no lag bin, and their semivariance is returned as zero_lag_semivariance. It refuses a variogram that falls with distance over its shorter lags, and a fitted range shorter than the shortest lag fitted, each with its own rejected_reason.

  • Every classed estimate_sac_range() result carries its nugget (attr(, "nugget")), whether the nugget sits at the bound of the fit (nugget_at_bound), the shortest lag resolved (first_lag) and the semivariance of nearest-neighbour pairs (short_lag_semivariance). It also keeps the four directional variograms with directional_status. The result gains a plot() method, and print() names the unit and the CRS of the range.

Choose a resolution

  • build_tessellation(approx_n_cells = ), get_voronoi_seeds(n = ), create_grid_polygons(target_cells = ) and create_grid_polygons_cached(target_cells = ) accept the ranked counts of determine_optimal_levels() (the first is used), a select_resolution() result or a resolution_profile(). Given a selection or a profile, the k-means seeding functions return the centres the profile scored.

  • determine_optimal_levels() gains on_no_elbow = c("na", "warn", "error") and select_on = c("all", "split"). "split" reads the response on one of two spatially blocked halves and returns the row positions of both, so estimates can be made on the half the selection never saw. resolution_profile() and select_features_forward() take select_on too. The model-aware criteria of determine_optimal_levels() now run with a response and no predictors.

Build the cells

  • build_tessellation() and create_voronoi_polygons() gain cover, the observations or polygon the cells must hold when the seeds were made elsewhere. Seeds with neither a boundary nor a cover raise a warning of class spatialkit_no_cover. A hex or square lattice records params$cells_occupied and params$cells_empty, and points snapped to a cell are recorded in params$snapped.

  • get_voronoi_seeds(method = "kmeans") and voronoi_seeds_kmeans() gain partition, init, density_power and density_k; voronoi_seeds_kmeans() also gains nstart and iter_max. A seeding that is not plain k-means from its own starts records itself in attr(, "partition"), and get_voronoi_seeds() returns its clustering as attr(, "kmeans").

Assign and summarise

  • assign_features_to_polygons() records the features no polygon holds as attr(, "unassigned") and the features a tie-break decided as attr(, "ties"). It names the column it read the polygon IDs from when polygon_id_col is absent, and the new quiet silences that message.

  • summarize_by_cell() gains estimate (pooled values by default), obs_level, conf_level and area. A pooled value is the cell’s mean pulled toward the mean of the observations in the 8 nearest cells. obs_level adds a range for one further observation in the cell, conf_level a t interval for the cell mean, and area = TRUE the cell’s area and a point density, refused where the CRS distorts areas across the cells by more than 1 percent. attr(, "intervals") says what each interval covers.

  • summarize_by_cell() returns more of what it computes: the Kish ICCs as attr(, "icc") whether or not they were applied, a deff_applied column whenever a design effect is requested, and under deff = "variogram" the per-cell design effects as deff_rows.

Make folds

  • make_folds() gains method = "knndm", k-fold nearest-neighbour distance matching (Linnenbrink et al. 2024), which has no row limit; max_test for "buffered_loo" and "nndm", which builds folds for a random subset of held-out points; blocks, a polygon layer to use as the blocks of "block_kfold"; and balance_tol, the fold-size ratio above which it warns that the folds are imbalanced.

  • make_folds(method = "block_kfold") returns the block design: a block_id column in assignment, and params$blocks (the block polygons), params$block_sizes and params$fold_blocks. plot_folds() draws the block outlines under the points (blocks = FALSE hides them), and its subtitle gives the size of the blocks built beside the block_size asked for, in the CRS’s unit.

Fit a model

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() reports what its GP basis resolves ($info$gp_resolution) and gains gp_resolution to ask for a finer one. After sampling, $info$gp_adequacy$status says whether the posterior shows structure the basis cannot represent, with a warning of class spatialkit_gp_adequacy when it does.

  • fit_gwr_model(predictor_vars = character(0)) fits a local intercept alone, the baseline a GWR with predictors has to beat. gwr_model_selection() scores it as <none> and gains delta, and its result has a plot() method. predict() on a GWR fit warns, with class spatialkit_gwr_extrapolation, when a location lies beyond the reach of every training kernel.

  • fit_gwr_model() surveys the collinearity of every fitting window (info$local_collinearity, with condition indices with and without the intercept), and plot(fit, type = "coefficients") maps one local coefficient, drawing the windows whose estimate is unstable hollow and grey (mask = FALSE draws them plainly).

  • fit_rf_model() gains replace and sample_fraction, passed to ranger::ranger() and recorded in $info. The defaults are ranger’s, so no forest changes.

Use a fitted model

  • coef() and predict() on a GWR fit give standard errors. coef(fit, se = TRUE) returns the local estimates with their standard errors and t values, and predict(fit, newdata, se.fit = TRUE) returns se.fit and se.pred. Both follow GWmodel’s definitions, treat the bandwidth as known, and make no adjustment for the number of local tests. print(summary(fit)) adds the effective number of parameters and a global least-squares fit on the same rows (info$global_ols).

  • plot(fit, type = "variogram") draws the response’s own variogram beside the residual variogram (response = FALSE draws the residuals alone).

Check a fit in sample

  • residual_morans_i() returns the weights it used as a one-line description (weights_summary) and the matrix itself only under the new keep_weights = TRUE, and its result has a print() method.

Cross-validate and compare

  • compare_models_cv() gains block_size and auto_range, passed to the shared folds; with the defaults the folds are those of 2.0.0. Its overall carries the Bayesian GP’s interval coverage and mean CRPS when that model runs.

  • Every cv_*() result accounts for each fold and row: fold_status (one row per fold: "ok", "error" with the error text, "skipped", "dropped" or "worker_error"), orphan_rows, n_unknown_ids and n_dropped.

  • cv_spatial(), cv_gwr(), cv_bayes(), cv_rf() and compare_models_cv() gain metrics, a scoring function of your own, function(y, yhat) returning a named numeric vector. It is applied per fold and to the pooled predictions, beside the built-in metrics.

Choose predictors

  • select_features_forward() gains null_fn, a function that fits the model with no predictors for a learner that cannot, and auto_range for its inner folds. history starts with the step-0 row and gains gain, fold_gain and fold_gain_se. The result gains baseline and fold_scores, carries the class "feature_selection", and has a plot() method.

Predict a surface

  • area_of_applicability() gains categorical = c("refuse", "indicator", "drop") for factor and character predictors, and coords, which sets whether location gets an index of its own. The result records the scaling of the predictors and the method of the folds its threshold came from (params$folds_method), and has a plot() method.

Bug fixes

Across the pipeline

  • Rows without a location were read as located, or stopped calls with a bare message. A row with an empty geometry, a coordinate that is NA, not finite or beyond 1e150, or a latitude beyond 90 in a geographic CRS now has no location wherever the package reads one, before and after any move to another CRS. prep_model_data() and the fits drop and count it, make_folds(), estimate_sac_range() and determine_optimal_levels() leave it out, coerce_to_points() gives it an empty point, assign_features_to_polygons() leaves it unassigned, the seeders drop it, and plot_tessellation_map() and plot_folds() leave it out with a warning. Layers without such rows give the same results.

  • Results on gridded locations changed with the unit and the origin of the coordinates. Where a point lay on a cell, block or kernel edge, or as near two neighbours, the last bits of its coordinates chose between them. The package now treats squared distances within one part in ten million as equal and breaks such ties in a fixed order (lower x, then lower y, then row). This applies to assign_features_to_polygons(), build_tessellation(), create_grid_polygons(), make_folds() (block, buffered and NNDM folds), estimate_sac_range(), residual_morans_i(), predict_surface() and the boxcar kernel of the GWR functions.

  • k-means seeds, Delaunay triangles and merged duplicates changed with the unit and the origin of the coordinates. get_voronoi_seeds(), voronoi_seeds_kmeans(), build_tessellation(method = "triangles") and create_voronoi_polygons() now hand stats::kmeans() and qhull the coordinates centred on their bounding box, divided by its diagonal and rounded to about a billionth of it, and merge points that round to one point there. On gridded locations the cells can differ from 2.0.0’s, and elsewhere the seeds can come in another order. build_tessellation(method = "triangles") no longer drops most points at UTM coordinates.

  • A response or predictor far from zero, or in very small or very large units, lost its spread to rounding. Tests for a constant column used absolute floors, and least-squares fits lost a predictor at a large offset. estimate_sac_range(), summarize_by_cell(), area_of_applicability(), residual_morans_i(), determine_optimal_levels(), the three fitters, select_features_forward() and the metrics now judge spread relative to the values, and centre a column whose centre is more than 1,000 times its spread. Results are those of the same values shifted to zero, to rounding.

  • Coordinates or a response too far from zero for doubles to hold a millionth of their spread raised no warning. make_folds(), assign_features_to_polygons(), create_grid_polygons(), create_voronoi_polygons(), build_tessellation() and clip_target_for() warn with class spatialkit_xy_imprecise where the spacing of doubles at the coordinates exceeds a millionth of the layer’s extent. prep_model_data(), and so every fit and cv_*() function, and estimate_sac_range() warn with class spatialkit_response_imprecise for such a response. Both say to shift the values nearer zero.

  • Several results depended on the order of the rows. determine_optimal_levels(), the n_max subsample of estimate_sac_range(), the deff_max_n subsample of summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram"), the normalizer_max_n subsample of area_of_applicability(), the max_n subsample of gp_lengthscale_bounds(), the sample ensure_projected() scores its candidates on, and the tie-breaks of assign_features_to_polygons() now put the rows in a fixed order first. Any permutation of a layer gives the same result. Fold numbers no longer depend on the machine’s collation: character fold labels are sorted in C order.

  • A layer that mixed XY and XYZ (or XYM) geometries, or whose geometries carry M, stopped calls or was read by its first row. sf and GEOS took the dimension of the first row, or stopped with “GEOS does not support XYM or XYZM geometries”. Every function now reads such layers in x and y. Where a copy of the caller’s rows comes back, as from coerce_to_points() or ensure_stable_poly_id(), it is XY, with a warning of class spatialkit_zm_dropped. fit_gwr_model() no longer mixes a Z coordinate into its distances.

  • A layer whose geometry column has the class sfc_GEOMETRY but holds only points stopped most functions with sf’s “not implemented for objects of class sfc_GEOMETRY”. sf::st_cast(x, "GEOMETRY") builds such a column. The fits, the cv_*() functions, make_folds(), summarize_by_cell(), the seeders, the tessellation builders and predict_surface() now read it as the same POINT or MULTIPOINT layer. A layer that mixes points with other geometry types is read as before.

  • A layer without a CRS could be stamped with the wrong one. A layer whose coordinates cannot be longitude and latitude is refused a geographic CRS, with an error that names the argument; 2.0.0 stamped it, and drew cells in metres at “latitude” 4,000,000. When only one of the points and the boundary has a CRS, the tessellation builders read the other in it, with a warning, where they stopped on sf’s “st_crs(x) == st_crs(y) is not TRUE”. create_voronoi_polygons() and the k-means seeders read CRS-less lon/lat points as lon/lat, as ensure_projected() does.

  • Lon/lat polygons that s2 refuses stopped calls with s2’s bare message, and some results changed with sf::sf_use_s2(). assign_features_to_polygons() stops with an error of class spatialkit_cells_degenerate that names the rows and says to transform the polygons to a projected CRS. ensure_projected(), coerce_to_points() and ensure_stable_poly_id() repair such polygons first. Areas, unions and sort keys in degrees are taken on the sphere whatever the session setting, so lwgeom is no longer needed with s2 off and the results are those of an s2 session.

  • A move to another CRS that could not place a row returned it emptied or short of a vertex, with no warning. harmonize_crs(), ensure_projected(target_crs = ) and every function that moves a layer it is given into the CRS of its data now warn with class spatialkit_rows_unplaced, naming the rows and the argument. The rows come back as before.

  • citation("spatialkit") gave the year it was called in, not the year of the release. It now reads the CRAN publication date, then Date, then the build date.

  • The plots’ size arguments did nothing on ggplot2 older than 3.4.0. Suggests now asks for ggplot2 (>= 3.4.0), and testthat (>= 3.1.7) for the test suite.

Prepare the data

  • coerce_to_points() ended the R session on an empty line feature, and on a lon/lat line its temporary projection could not place. An empty feature now gives an empty POINT, and a line the projection cannot place in full stops with an error of class spatialkit_features_degenerate that offers mode = "centroid" or tmp_project = FALSE. A centroid that falls outside the bounding box of an invalid projected polygon stops with the same class.

  • coerce_to_points() put the point of a lon/lat geometry written across longitude 180 on the far side of the globe. Points on the surface, box centres and planar centroids now read such a geometry’s longitudes from 0 to 360 and bring the point back into -180 to 180. sf’s warning “st_point_on_surface may not give correct results for longitude/latitude data” is no longer passed on, since the point lies on the polygon as ?coerce_to_points describes.

  • coerce_to_points() put line midpoints off the middle in a CRS whose unit sf has no name for. sf::st_line_sample() measures such a line in metres, so in a unit of 2 m a line’s midpoint landed at its end. The midpoint is now taken at half the planar length in the CRS’s own unit. Among parts of a MULTILINESTRING of equal greatest length, the midpoint lowest in x, then y, is taken. The error for mode = "line_midpoint" names mode, where it said method.

  • ensure_projected() chose its projection from rows that should not decide it. The candidates are now scored on a sample of the distinct locations sorted by coordinate. Pairs shorter than 1 mm, rows without a location and rows with Z or M coordinates (scored as their XY copy) no longer shape the score, and a candidate that cannot place every vertex is not chosen. Data wholly on one side of the equator get a Lambert azimuthal projection centred on the pole where it distorts distances less than Web Mercator. The chosen CRS can differ from 2.0.0’s on such layers.

  • ensure_projected() stopped with “invalid crs” on some lon/lat layers. A layer whose box has no height and whose centre lies within 5 degrees of a pole gave an Albers candidate with a parallel beyond 90; such a candidate is now left out. Its warning on a layer across a pole, or with longitudes outside -180 to 180, gave an offset from the UTM zone’s central meridian beyond 180 degrees; the offset is now wrapped.

  • harmonize_crs() refused an sf layer as target_crs. An sf or sfc target now means its CRS. The tessellation builders take an sf layer as crs in the same way.

Measure spatial autocorrelation

  • estimate_sac_range() drew its n_max subsample over rows with nothing to model, and fitted the raw response when one value was infinite. Rows with a missing or non-finite response or predictor are now left out of the subsample, the detrending fit and the variogram, with a logged count.

  • estimate_sac_range() returned NA or an R error for a bad argument without naming it. cutoff, range_frac, n_max and seed are checked, and a bad value is an error that names the argument; cutoff above 1 and n_max below 30 are errors. With range_frac below 1, the reason for a refused range no longer says that it exceeded the largest lag.

  • print() on an estimate_sac_range() result showed a bare number. It now names the unit and the CRS of the range (“in metres of EPSG:32617”) and whether the variogram is of the response or of its residuals.

Choose a resolution

  • determine_optimal_levels() read a misspelt response_var or predictor_vars as absent and changed the criterion. A named column that is not in the layer is now an error. A model-aware criterion given no predictors, or no response, says which is missing in an R warning.

  • determine_optimal_levels() dropped Moran’s I when a few predictor values were missing. Rows with a missing or non-finite response or predictor now stay in the WSS sweep and the cells and are left out of Moran’s I, with a logged count.

  • determine_optimal_levels() stopped one count short when locations repeat. Its cap is now the number of distinct locations. On five stations visited many times it warned of no cluster structure and returned other counts; it now returns the stations’ count first.

  • determine_optimal_levels(criterion = "morans_i") gave a count different cells when top_n or max_levels changed. Each count’s re-run is now seeded from one integer drawn before the sweep plus the count, so for one set_seed a count gets the same cells in any window that holds it. With set_seed = NULL the re-runs no longer draw from the caller’s stream.

  • determine_optimal_levels() returned 1 for a layer with no rows. It is now an error.

Build the cells

  • build_tessellation() with a geographic crs built every method in degrees. The cells are now built and indexed in the projected CRS ensure_projected() picks, then returned in the geographic CRS with long edges densified, and Delaunay triangles hold their own points. Over a near-global boundary, where that CRS distorts areas by more than 1 percent, create_grid_polygons() and the hex and square lattices use the equal-area CRS ensure_projected(purpose = "area") picks, not Web Mercator.

  • build_tessellation() on cells in degrees held its snap tolerance in degrees against distances in metres, and stopped with “there is no package called ‘lwgeom’” with s2 off. The tolerance is now an arc of the sphere, and the snap is taken on the sphere whatever sf::sf_use_s2() says.

  • build_tessellation(method = "triangles") gave an empty triangulation for collinear points and recorded an approx_n_cells it had ignored. It now stops with a message that says the points are collinear and points to method = "voronoi", and params$approx_n_cells is NULL. A warning says that approx_n_cells and cellsize size only the hex and square lattices.

  • build_tessellation() and create_voronoi_polygons() failed on a whole build_tessellation() result passed as boundary with sf’s “no applicable method for ‘st_geometry’”. The error now says to pass its $boundary. clip_target_for() and make_folds() refuse a boundary that is not an sf or sfc layer by name.

  • clip_target_for() returned the wrong target for points far from the origin, very close together or without a location. Far from the origin it returned disks around points whose bounding box it should return; points less than about 3e-153 apart got a point or an empty line; points none of which has a location stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”. The box is now read against its span, near-coincident points get the same disk as points at one location, and points with no location are refused. The message for points at one location gives the radius and its unit.

  • create_grid_polygons() sized grids badly in three cases. A transect with sub-millimetre scatter got a sliver study area and a grid of many times the cells asked for; a box whose short side is below a millionth of the long side is now treated as degenerate. Hex cell size depended on which way the boundary lay. A side that is a whole number of cells got an extra row of slivers in some units. A clip that leaves no cell is now an error.

  • create_grid_polygons() ignored target_cells, with no warning, when cellsize or n was also given. cellsize and n still win, and a logged warning now says that target_cells was ignored.

  • create_grid_polygons_cached() could return another site’s grid, or a grid that differs from create_grid_polygons()’s. The cache key now hashes the CRS’s WKT and, for a grid returned in degrees, the sf::sf_use_s2() setting. With crs given, the cached grid is the one ensure_stable_poly_id(create_grid_polygons()) returns. target_cells defaults to NULL, so cellsize = or n = work without it.

  • create_voronoi_polygons() and build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") grew a small layer’s hull too much in coarse units. The margin is 2 percent of the diagonal of the hull’s bounding box, but the diagonal was floored at 1 CRS unit, so a layer less than 1 unit across, such as a small layer in a kilometre CRS, grew by more. The margin is now 2 percent of the diagonal in every unit. Layers whose diagonal is 1 unit or more get the same cells.

  • create_voronoi_polygons() and build_tessellation(method = "voronoi") with expand > 0 returned the boundary before it was grown, and dropped a clipped cell that also touched the boundary from outside, leaving its points in no cell. They now return the grown boundary and keep each cell’s polygonal part. A seed outside a boundary that is not convex gets its cell in index, where it got NA.

  • ensure_stable_poly_id() failed on, or moved, valid polygons. It stopped on a cell that is valid in its own CRS and crosses itself in lon/lat, which also stopped build_tessellation(method = "voronoi"). It moved the corners of valid polygons in degrees with s2 on, numbered a layer far from its CRS’s origin by the row order, and turned empty polygons into lines. It now repairs only the rows s2 or GEOS calls invalid, measures the rest as given, and returns empty polygons as they came.

  • get_voronoi_seeds() ignored seeds under method = "kmeans" and "random", and sample_points under "random", with no warning. It now warns that the method ignores the argument. Random and k-means seeding on a lon/lat boundary no longer warn “install package lwgeom” on every call.

  • plot_tessellation_map() failed at print on some columns. A fill column of units, Date, POSIXct or difftime values is now drawn on a continuous or time scale, a units label is drawn with its unit, and a cell with an NA ID or an empty geometry gets no label. On lon/lat layers the labels no longer warn at print.

  • voronoi_seeds_kmeans() gave the distinct positions as the reason for a clamp set by the number of points. The warning now uses the words of get_voronoi_seeds() for the same clamp, and both give a count that is not whole as requested. voronoi_seeds_kmeans(k = ), voronoi_seeds_random(k = ) and a malformed expand are refused by name.

  • voronoi_seeds_random() and get_voronoi_seeds() stopped, ran out of memory or never returned on some boundaries. They exhausted memory on a boundary whose bounding box is far larger than its area, stopped on a lon/lat boundary of small pieces far apart or with crossing edges, and never returned on a lon/lat ring along a parallel. Such boundaries are now sampled piece by piece, repaired, or refused at once with the remedy. A boundary row with a latitude beyond 90, or whose repair leaves no polygon, is refused or left out.

Assign and summarise

  • assign_features_to_polygons() let invalid polygons change the join. One invalid polygon switched the whole layer to another assignment rule, and the smallest-area tie-break took a polygon whose ring crosses itself as the smallest. Invalid features and cells are now repaired with sf::st_make_valid() for the join only, with a warning that counts them.

  • assign_features_to_polygons() joined lon/lat features to projected cells on bent cell edges. The join now runs in the cells’ CRS whenever it is projected, and the features come back with their own geometry, so lon/lat points near a cell edge can change cell to match a join done in the projected CRS.

  • assign_features_to_polygons() let the row order of polygons_sf decide ties. tie_break = "smallest_area" decides equal areas by the lowest, then leftmost, centre, and largest = TRUE decides an exact tie in overlap by tie_break; a feature its rules cannot place is left unassigned with a warning of class spatialkit_ties_unresolved. With largest = TRUE a polygon feature that only touches the cells is unassigned, and sf’s “attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant” warning is muffled.

  • assign_features_to_polygons() dropped the features’ own id column when the cells were keyed by id. Only a column named polygon_id_col is replaced now. With s2 off in degrees the join no longer needs lwgeom.

  • summarize_by_cell() let infinite values and malformed arguments through. An infinite value is now left out of every statistic of its column, with a warning of class spatialkit_nonfinite. A deff that is not a single finite number of at least 1 falls back to 1 with a warning, a deff_max_n below 2 is an error, and a misspelt or non-numeric response_var or predictor, which was dropped, now raises a warning.

  • summarize_by_cell(cells_sf = ) lost or missed cells. A double cell ID of 100000 lost its cell, because whole numbers were written in scientific notation; they are now written in full. The cells are now searched for the ID columns assign_features_to_polygons() writes, and a summarised ID that matches no cell is reported with a warning.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram") misread the variogram it was given. It read an anisotropic variogram as isotropic, ignored a sac that carried no variogram model, said “Falling back to deff = 1” for a rejected sac and then applied a design effect, and corrected the response with a residual variogram. Each case now applies the model as gstat does, or says in a warning what it used instead.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram") mishandled empty points and calls without a value column. An empty point gave its cell a design effect of 1; such points now count towards their cell’s values and not towards its correlation. A call with no value column now returns the counts and cell_weight, where it stopped, and each cell’s correlation matrix is built fewer times.

  • summarize_by_cell() recorded corrections wrongly. The rows with no cell ID got a cell_weight of 0, a fixed deff with one populated cell recorded attr(, "deff_applied")$deff as NA, and deff = "kish" recorded no correction when only the predictors were corrected. Each is now counted and recorded as for any other cell or correction.

Make folds

  • make_folds(drop_empty_blocks = FALSE) could return folds with no test points. k is now lowered to the number of blocks that hold points. Wherever make_folds() returns fewer folds than k ("random_kfold" with more folds than rows, "block_kfold" with fewer occupied blocks than k, "leave_location_out" with more folds than groups), its warning gives a setting that works.

  • make_folds(method = "block_kfold") built uneven or degenerate grids. The automatic grid gave an east-west corridor more than twice the blocks of the same corridor running north-south; both now get the same count. block_nx or block_ny given alone was ignored and is now used, with the other derived from the extent. A boundary that is not rectangular left zero-area slivers as blocks; only the areal part of the grid is kept.

  • make_folds() checked arguments with R’s own errors or not at all. A missing k, an invalid buffer, any block_multiplier, and a units object for buffer, block_size, block_nx, block_ny, phi or min_train are now refused by name. The refusal of a grid above 1,000,000 blocks names what produced it, where it blamed a block_size the caller never passed.

  • make_folds() gave its warnings about range and leakage too rarely, or with advice that failed. The leakage warning of "block_kfold" now fires whenever a response_var is available, since a range is estimated for it alone, and its advice gives settings that build k folds. auto_range = TRUE falling back to geometric blocks, "buffered_loo" with a buffer that excludes no neighbour, and NNDM folds left short of their target by min_train now raise R warnings.

  • make_folds(method = "nndm") returned plain leave-one-out without a warning when the prediction points were nearer the data than leave-one-out reaches. A warning of class spatialkit_nndm_out_of_reach now says that the cross-validated error is an upper bound for those locations. NNDM also frees its neighbour tables as soon as it has them, lowering its peak memory.

  • plot_folds() failed at print when its layers disagreed on having a CRS. A layer without a CRS is now brought into the points’ CRS, as make_folds() does: reprojected from lon/lat when its coordinates look like it, stamped with a warning otherwise.

Fit a model

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() accepted families and responses it could not score. A two-level factor response under brms::bernoulli() is now refused before compiling, brms::categorical() and mixture() families fit, and predict() on an ordinal or categorical fit stops with advice where it returned NA as a “posterior draw failed”. cv_bayes() refuses the ordinal and categorical families before sampling any fold.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() returned fits it should have refused, and called an unchecked fit converged. A fit with no posterior draws is now an error, and a response of one value stops before compiling. check_convergence = FALSE sets convergence_ok to NA, where it read TRUE, and the convergence check no longer raises dozens of “The ESS has been capped” warnings.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() sized gp_k for the default gp_c whatever gp_c was set to. With gp_k = NULL the derived gp_k now matches the gp_c used. The cached fitted values of a fit can no longer come from another model.

  • fit_gwr_model() judged collinearity on a predictor’s origin. It called windows collinear because of where a predictor’s units start (a temperature in kelvin against degrees C), never checked a one-predictor model, and raised false warnings for a predictor named twice. The global and local indices are now computed on centred predictors.

  • fit_gwr_model() capped an adaptive bandwidth above the number of points with no warning, could choose a bandwidth at which a term is estimable at no location, and let local regressions that interpolate the data win on AICc. It now warns of the cap, skips such bandwidths, and reports the AICc of an interpolating fit as NA; gwr_model_selection() ranks such models last.

  • fit_gwr_model() accepted a character or factor response. It now stops with “response ‘y’ is not numeric”, as fit_rf_model() and fit_bayesian_spatial_model() do. Below 20 points, bandwidth = NULL now fits at the bandwidth the search chose. print() shows a fixed bandwidth with its unit and an adaptive one as a number of neighbours.

  • fit_rf_model() hid ranger’s errors. ranger wrote its diagnosis to stderr and threw “User interrupt or internal error”; the error now carries ranger’s reason, and predict() on a forest stops with it, where it returned all NA. A forest in which every tree sampled some rows, so they have no out-of-bag prediction, now warns with the count. The include_coords = TRUE caution prints once per session, also under cv_rf().

  • A fit saved from fit_rf_model() or fit_bayesian_spatial_model() carried its engine twice, through the environment of its formula. The formulas now carry the global environment, as one typed at the console does.

Use a fitted model

  • plot() on a fit failed in two cases. A custom spatial_fit without a residuals() method stopped with “could not extract residuals”; its residuals are now the response minus fitted(). The subtitle of type = "variogram" ran off the figure, and is now wrapped.

  • predict() on a GWR fit lost every prediction to one location it could not estimate. Predictions now come from the package’s own local regressions, one per new location, and only a location with no estimable prediction is NA, with a warning that counts them.

  • predict() on a Bayesian GP fit let one row spoil the others. A row of newdata with a factor level the model was not fitted with made every row NA; now that row alone is NA, with a warning of class spatialkit_new_levels. On brms 2.17 to 2.22 one far-off row moved every prediction; the GP boundary is now held at its fitted value, and a row beyond it is NA with a warning.

Check a fit in sample

  • compare_models() set unlike numbers side by side. It put LOOIC and AICc of fits on different rows, or of different responses, in one column, and out-of-bag forest metrics beside in-sample ones, unlabelled. Such columns are now NA with a warning, and a metric_basis column says what each row is computed on. A significantly negative residual Moran’s I is no longer read as missed spatial structure.

  • compare_models() and evaluate_insample() failed on a list holding no spatial_fit. Both now stop with an error that names fits. compare_models(fits, newdata = ) no longer labels training-residual Moran’s I as a newdata metric.

  • model_metrics() and the scores read the response’s units. R² against newdata used another baseline than the cv_*() functions; it now uses the training mean. R², MAPE and RMSE were NA or wrong for a response in very small or very large units, or whose squares overflow. A character or factor response is an error, where it gave n = 0 and every metric NA, and draws = TRUE is refused by name.

  • residual_morans_i() accepted inputs it could not use. k was not checked, a weights matrix with NA or Inf aborted inside a guard, an empty geometry kept its row, and a custom fit without a residuals() method had no statistic. Each is now refused by name or handled: empty rows are dropped with a count, and a custom fit is scored on the response minus fitted(), as plot() scores it.

Cross-validate and compare

  • compare_models_cv() ranked models scored on different rows. When the predicted rows differ, every model is now rescored on the rows all of them predicted, with a warning; overall carries n_pred. The shared blocks place polygon rows by the same point every model is fitted at.

  • The cv_*() functions ignored block_size and auto_range = TRUE, with no warning, when folds was supplied. They now raise a warning of class spatialkit_fold_args_ignored. cv_rf(parallel = ) prints its core-count message once.

  • cv_bayes() rounded coverage levels to a whole percent, so close levels overwrote each other, and every CRPS was NA above 46,340 posterior draws. Columns are now named at full precision (coverage_97.5), a level outside (0, 1) or given twice is an error, and the CRPS is computed in double precision.

  • cv_gwr(parallel = n) hung once a GWR had been fitted in the session. It now runs its folds one after another whenever parallel would fork, and says so in a warning.

  • cv_spatial() checked too little of what a fold’s fit returns. It scored a fold’s predictions against response_var without checking that the fit models it, failed after every fold when ..per_row came back from some folds only, and let a ..per_row column overwrite predictions. Each case now fails the fold or the call with a message, and the error of a fold_info_fn is named in fold_status$message.

  • cv_spatial(), cv_rf(), cv_gwr() and cv_bayes() lost folds with no warning. When some folds failed, overall left them out without a warning, and a parallel run discarded the folds that shared a worker with a failure. Each fold now runs in its own worker, and the functions warn, naming the failed folds and the rows overall covers. Re-using a result’s $folds keeps its fold numbers.

  • cv_spatial() and the other cv_*() functions checked folds saved by spatialkit 2.0.0 by a rule that sf::sf_use_s2() changed. Saved folds on lon/lat polygons were refused after the setting was toggled, folds built on a pointized copy of a polygon layer were refused as built from other data, and on data with a polygon s2 refuses they were applied without a check. The check now gives the same answer under either setting.

Choose predictors

  • gwr_model_selection() failed with bare messages on some inputs. A layer with no rows stopped with an sp error, a fixed bandwidth in the wrong units with “inv(): matrix is singular”, and an adaptive bandwidth was checked less strictly than in fit_gwr_model(). Each is now refused in fit_gwr_model()’s words.

  • select_features_forward() could pick a variable for making folds fail. Every candidate is now scored on one fixed set of rows, a set that leaves any of them unpredicted scores NA with a warning, and history gains n_pred.

  • select_features_forward() did not say when fit_fn ignored the variables it was handed. Two predictor sets that score the same to the last digit at the first step now raise a warning that names the fix. The same data warning is no longer repeated for every candidate set.

Predict a surface

  • area_of_applicability() returned a threshold of 0 from repeat visits or duplicated training rows. Without folds a row’s reference is now its nearest row with different predictor values; with folds a threshold of 0 raises a warning of class spatialkit_aoa_zero_threshold with the remedy. Without FNN, exact copies of training rows get a distance of 0.

  • area_of_applicability() marked some extrapolation as inside. Rows that differ from the training data on a predictor with no training variance now get DI = Inf and count outside, and a fractional chunk_size is refused. All-zero weights, which pmax(importance, 0) gives when no predictor helped, now give equal weights with a warning, where they were refused.

  • area_of_applicability() refused or misapplied folds. Folds built before prep_model_data() dropped a row stopped it with “fold 1 refers to rows outside 1:n”; the dropped rows are now taken out, as the cv_*() functions take them out. Folds built on other rows are refused with the cv_*() message, and character fold labels are numbered as there.

  • predict_surface() built its grid and took covariates from the wrong points. A polygon grid took covariates from an arbitrary point in each cell, the automatic grid could lose a column or row and left part of the training extent uncovered to the east and north, and a reused grid kept its old .pred_se. The grid is now reduced to one point per cell, covers the box, and is centred on it. draws = TRUE is refused by name.

Set options, catch conditions and clear caches

  • Logging could abort or hide the package’s messages. A logger configuration made before loading the package could abort its functions and receive its log lines, and deleting the session’s temporary directory made every function that logs fail. Logging is now isolated and never aborts the caller, and logged cautions appear in knitted documents as R messages.

  • create_grid_polygons_cached() kept an entry for every cache_env it was given after that environment was gone. A fresh cache_env per call left one entry behind each time; a finalizer now removes it with its environment.

Documentation

  • The documentation is published as a website at https://elkronos.github.io/gis_modeling_toolkit/, with the home page, every help page grouped by pipeline step, the articles and this changelog. The articles are grouped as Get started, Step by step, Worked example and Help, and formulas on the help pages render as mathematics.

  • Eight articles join the North Carolina example: “Get started”, “Choosing a resolution”, “Building cells and summarising them”, “Spatial cross-validation”, “Fitting and checking models”, “Exporting and reporting results”, “Troubleshooting and performance” and “Terms used on these pages”. Those with code run when the site is built and skip the parts whose optional packages are absent. vignette("spatialkit_nc_demo") is retitled “Worked example: North Carolina” and matches its own output. The site’s earlier Diagnostics article is split between the cells and models articles, and its address now leads to “Fitting and checking models”.

  • The reference index follows the pipeline, from preparing the data to predicting a surface, and the “See also” of every help page lists the other functions in its section of the index. Three help topics are new: ?"spatialkit-geometry" (how input geometry is read), ?"spatialkit-conditions" (every condition class, what it means and what to do) and ?"spatialkit-options" (the two options that bound the package’s work).

  • Ten numbered scripts are installed in system.file("scripts", package = "spatialkit"), each covering one topic on a simulated field with known structure; 00-run-all.R runs them in order. SPATIALKIT_TOUR_OUTPUT writes their figures to a folder and SPATIALKIT_TOUR_PAUSE = "no" skips the pause after each figure. The home page is generated from README.Rmd, so its figures and numbers are computed when it is built.

  • The help pages and articles describe a cross-validated error as the error at the distance the folds put between held-out points and their training data. Random folds give the error of predicting among the samples, and blocks give the error of predicting into gaps of their size. The pages no longer call random folds optimistic or the blocked score the one to report. fold_separation() compares the folds with the locations of the map you will predict.

  • ?summarize_by_cell says what ..se_* covers at each deff: at the default deff = 1, the cell’s own mean when its observations are spread through the cell; under "kish", "variogram" or a number, the cell mean as an estimate of the population mean. The numbers are those of 2.0.0.

  • ?select_features_forward says that $score is the cross-validated metric of the winning set, which the selection itself flatters, and not an estimate of how the selected model performs. Running the selection inside cv_spatial()’s fit_fn gives that estimate.

  • ?fit_bayesian_spatial_model gains a section on spatial confounding, and ?model_metrics says which metrics suit a response that is not Gaussian: RMSE and MAE suit any numeric response, and cv_bayes()’s CRPS and interval coverage are the proper scores for counts and bounded responses.

spatialkit 2.0.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-11

Everything below is relative to 1.0.0 (published on CRAN 2026-08-07). Three exported functions are removed and several defaults change results; read Breaking changes before upgrading.

These notes describe what changed for a user of 1.0.0.

Throughout, raises a warning means a genuine R warning(), which tryCatch(warning = ) catches, suppressWarnings() suppresses and options(warn = 2) escalates. Logs a warning means a logger message in the "spatialkit" namespace, which none of those touch.

Breaking changes

Corrections that change results

  • residual_morans_i() no longer puts weight on a point’s own residual. FNN::get.knn() reports a point’s OWN index among its neighbours whenever exact duplicate coordinates are present, which put 1/k on the diagonal of a matrix Moran’s I is only defined for with a zero diagonal. On 40 sites x 4 repeats with a response carrying no spatial structure, 120 of 160 rows gained a self-weight, mean I came out at +0.086 against E[I] = -0.0063, and 77% of samples were “significant” at p < 0.05 against a nominal 5%. Repeat observations at one site are exactly what make_folds(method = "leave_location_out") is for. The dense fallback never had the fault, so the statistic also depended silently on whether FNN happened to be installed; the two paths now share one neighbour lookup and agree exactly.

    Requesting k + 1 neighbours and dropping self is not sufficient on its own; the slot self occupied displaced a genuine co-located neighbour and left a farther point standing in for it (75 of 400 retained pairs sat at distance 121 where a neighbour at distance 0 existed). Duplicate coordinates are now grouped and answered exactly.

  • residual_morans_i() gains a null argument, defaulting to "auto". Model residuals are not exchangeable (they are orthogonal to the design matrix) so the classical randomisation moments are wrong for them. At n = 120 with six smooth covariates and independent errors, OLS residuals had mean I = -0.031 against the exchangeable E[I] = -0.008, and the z-score averaged -0.54 with sd 0.90 instead of 0 and 1. The Cliff & Ord (1981, sec. 8.3) regression-residual moments restore mean z = -0.09, sd 1.03 and a 4.3% rejection rate against a nominal 5%, and agree with spdep::lm.morantest() to machine precision (verified at 1e-16 through the public function). "auto" applies them only when the fit’s residuals really are the OLS residuals on the rebuilt design, which a forest’s and a working GWR’s are not; the null actually used is reported in the return value.

  • summarize_by_cell() standard errors under a design effect were too small. s / sqrt(n / deff) corrects the mean’s variance for clustering but leaves s^2 biased low by the same clustering: for exchangeable correlation rho, E[s^2] = sigma^2 (n - deff)/(n - 1). The two errors compound. Measured 95% CI coverage at n = 20: 0.905 at rho = 0.3, 0.796 at rho = 0.6, 0.632 at rho = 0.8; after rescaling by sqrt((n-1)/(n-deff)), 0.952 / 0.952 / 0.953. Applies to deff = "kish", deff = "variogram" and a fixed numeric deff. The default deff = 1 path is bit-identical to before.

  • determine_optimal_levels() ranks model-aware candidates on the standardised deviate, not on |Moran’s I|. E[I] and Var(I) both depend on the cell count, so |I| shrinks as k grows whether or not the finer tessellation captures anything. Over 300 replicates of a response with no spatial structure, mean |I| fell monotonically from 0.114 at k = 10 to 0.050 at k = 60; an |I| ranking prefers the largest candidate for arithmetic reasons alone. Candidates are now ordered by |z| using the Cliff & Ord residual moments (exact here, since the cell-level residuals are OLS residuals by construction); over the same runs z had mean ~0, sd ~1 and a 5% rejection rate of 0.040-0.057 at every k. The "diagnostics" attribute now carries moran_z alongside moran_i.

  • estimate_sac_range() sweeps four azimuths, not two. A +/-22.5 degree window around 0 and 90 covers exactly 90 of the 180 distinct azimuths; every direction between 23 and 67 degrees, and between 113 and 157, fell into neither. On simulated fields with 3:1 anisotropy and a true major-axis range of 300, the estimate came back at 255 and 249 for major axes at 0 and 90 degrees but 151 and 147 at 45 and 135. Since make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) sizes blocks from this number, a diagonally oriented field silently got blocks half as wide as the correlation they were meant to separate. c(0, 45, 90, 135) tiles all 180 azimuths; the same fields now return 255 / 245 / 249 /

    1. A direction whose variogram never reaches a sill is excluded rather than taken as a long range, and the directional attribute now has four named entries.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model()’s calibrated length-scale prior never reached Stan. brms::set_prior(spec, class = "lscale") with no coef is a global prior, and brms applies a global prior only to coefficients with no individual prior of their own; every lscale coefficient always has one. brms dropped it with a note and Stan received brms’s defaults, which made gp_lengthscale_bounds(), the tail calibration and $info$gp_lscale_prior dead weight. Confirmed with brms::make_stancode(): the requested prior is absent under the global form and present under the coefficient-level form, which is now used. $info$gp_lscale_prior is read back from brms::validate_prior(), so it records what brms will actually use.

  • The GP basis was sized against the wrong domain measure. brms builds the boundary as choose_L(x, c) = c * max(1, max(x) - min(x)) over the pooled, column-centred covariates, the full range, not the per-axis half-range in which Riutort-Mayol et al. state their inequalities. Recovering the boundary from make_standata()’s eigenvalues confirms L = c * full range exactly at every c, so the old convention built a boundary twice as wide as gp_k was sized for: the GP was under-resolved, and $info$gp_ell_min (the diagnostic meant to catch exactly that) was twice too lenient to fire. The c floor is now brms’s own default 1.25 rather than 1.2.

  • fitted() on a gwr_fit could return a coefficient surface. The search for GWmodel’s fitted-value column matched the whole candidate name vector with %in% and took the first hit in the SDF’s column order, and the local coefficients come first. A predictor named fit, pred, prediction, fitted or yhat therefore returned its own coefficient column, silently: executed in-sample R^2 was -1.18 against a true 0.981, and residuals(), summary(), model_metrics(), compare_models() and every cv_gwr() fold consumed it without a warning. The search now runs in preference order and excludes any candidate that is also a model term; all five colliding names now give R^2 = 0.981, identical to the renamed control.

  • coef.gwr_fit() returned GWmodel’s whole SDF data slot: 15 columns for a two-predictor fit, of which 3 are coefficients and the rest are standard errors, t-values, the response, the fitted values, residuals and Local_R2. It now returns the model terms only; reach for object$engine$SDF for the rest.

  • estimate_sac_range() is reproducible, and no longer disturbs the caller’s RNG. seed now defaults to 123L rather than NULL. The n_max subsample is an internal approximation, not part of the answer, and leaving it unseeded made the returned range differ between runs on identical input (19531 / 19589 / 19605 on three calls) while silently advancing the caller’s stream, and make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) sizes its blocks from that number. Pass seed = NULL for the old behaviour.

  • estimate_sac_range() rejects a non-numeric response. as.numeric() on a factor returns its level codes, so a factor response produced a variogram of an arbitrary integer relabelling of the categories and the estimated range changed when the levels were reordered (3700 against 2497 on the same data). Factors and character columns are now an error naming the column; logicals are read as 0/1.

  • Fold sets built from a different dataset are refused. Fold splits are lists of ..row_id values, and row IDs are seq_len(nrow()) unless supplied, so passing cv_gwr() a folds object built from another dataset of the same size applied cleanly; every ID matched, every fold was populated, and the model was scored on splits describing other observations. make_folds() now records a small projection-invariant row fingerprint in params$row_probe, and cv_gwr(), cv_bayes(), cv_spatial() and cv_rf() error rather than proceed. Fold objects from earlier versions carry no fingerprint and are passed through unchecked.

  • evaluate_insample() rejects duplicated names in fits. model is the key compare_models() joins its metric and Moran’s I tables on, so two fits called "GWR" produced a 2x2 cross-join: four rows, every one carrying the first fit’s numbers, with the second fit never scored at all.

  • fit_gwr_model() rejects a non-numeric predictor. gwr.basic() expands contrasts via model.matrix() and fits, but gwr.predict() does not and fails, so the model appeared to fit and then silently predicted all NA.

  • fit_gwr_model() no longer rejects a two-valued continuous response. The “binary” error is now gated on the response being integer-like. A left-censored or saturated measurement (every observation at a detection limit or a ceiling) has two distinct values and is perfectly continuous; it now warns instead. The guard also runs once per fold inside cv_gwr(), where a small training fold can legitimately hold only two distinct values.

  • fitted() returning the wrong length, or nothing, is now an error in summary() and model_metrics() rather than a plausible row count over an all-NA comparison. new_spatial_fit() is the documented extension point, so a subclass with a missing or mis-sized fitted() method is user-reachable.

  • The cached fitted() on a bayesian_fit is stamped with the n and a digest of the data it was computed from. The cache environment has reference semantics (which is what makes it survive copy-on-modify) so fit2 <- fit gave both objects the same cache, and assigning different data to the copy returned the original’s values at the original’s length.

  • make_folds() drops rows with empty or non-finite coordinates, with a logged warning naming the count, rather than letting an EMPTY POINT reach block_kfold’s nearest-block rescue and die with “replacement has length zero”.

  • When every fold fails, the warning now names the first underlying error. Previously “all 5 folds failed” was the whole diagnosis even when the cause was simply that brms or GWmodel was not installed.

  • make_folds() records the CRS the folds were built in as params$crs. Geographic input is projected by ensure_projected() to a CRS the caller never chose, and block_size, sac_range and buffer are lengths in that CRS.

  • .morans_i_for_k() returns NA at or below nine cells, where every cell neighbours every other and Moran’s I collapses to exactly -1/(k-1) for any residual vector, a function of the cell count alone.

  • residual_morans_i(fit, k = 1) works on machines without FNN. apply() simplified the length-1 result to a vector, making the neighbour index a 1 x n matrix and every row after the first out of bounds.

  • summarize_by_cell(deff = "kish") under-estimated the predictor ICC by about a factor of m. The pooled one-way ANOVA grouped the m z-scored predictor columns under the same cell label, so independent per-column cell effects averaged away in the shared cell mean and the between-cell sum of squares shrank by ~1/m. Measured at true rho = 0.5 with m = 4: pooled ICC 0.12 against 0.495 per column, so every predictor SE was ~44% too small. The pooled group is now (variable, cell), which recovers 0.49.

  • Design effects are built from what a column actually observes. A cell of 10 rows with 2 finite responses had its response SE formed at the 10-row design effect, then applied to a 2-observation mean: adding 8 NA-response rows moved the SE from 8.46 to 26.38. Each column’s design effect now uses its own non-missing count, with the mean pairwise correlation recomputed over the observed locations when a cell has NAs; cell_weight is the effective count of the primary variable, not of rows (n still counts rows).

  • CRS-less coordinates get ONE interpretation, wherever they enter. prep_model_data() assumed EPSG:4326 for CRS-less data that looked like lon/lat and projected it, while every predict() method passed the fit’s CRS as a target, a branch that stamped it onto the raw numbers. The same rows sat in two different places, and predict(fit, newdata = training rows) disagreed with fitted(fit) by up to one response SD (R² 0.98 in-sample, 0.64 via newdata). The heuristic is now a single function used by both branches; a fit records the assumption it was built under and replays it on CRS-less newdata. Two further symptoms of the same split, CRS-less LINESTRINGs aborting in coerce_to_points() (“crs not found”), and hex/square build_tessellation() refusing input voronoi accepted, are fixed with it. The assumption is now announced with a real R warning.

  • residual_morans_i() refuses a malformed weights matrix instead of silently substituting the default k-NN(8) matrix (I = 0.874 returned for four malformed shapes against 0.805 for the weights actually supplied).

  • The fold-provenance fingerprint no longer refuses the caller’s own data. Three defects in the version introduced last pass: a character ..row_id was coerced to all-NA (and matched row 1 everywhere); coordinates were compared as "%.7g" strings and flipped on the ~1 in 5000 that a reprojection moved by 5e-9°; and polygon input was probed after pointization, so a different pointize in the cv call read as different data. Both sides now probe the geometry as supplied, keep IDs in their own type, and compare numerically within 1e-6°.

  • n_folds_attempted counts the folds supplied. A fold whose test rows were all removed as incomplete vanished before fitting and was absent from both counts, so five supplied folds reported 4/4. It is announced with a real warning.

  • determine_optimal_levels()’s elbow uses the signed deviation below the chord. abs() let a concave bump above the chord (a k where k-means fell into a worse local optimum) win with the same magnitude.

  • estimate_sac_range() returns NA for a constant variable (an exactly explained response, or a constant one) instead of a fitted “range” of 168 or 673 from a variogram that is identically zero. make_folds(auto_range = TRUE) no longer re-opens the unseeded subsample by forwarding its own seed = NULL.

  • fit_bayesian_spatial_model() attaches a user-supplied global lscale prior at coefficient level, the same way it does its own, so set_prior(..., class = "lscale") reaches Stan instead of being discarded.

  • fitted() on a gwr_fit returns the prediction when a predictor is named prediction. The model-term exclusion added last pass was applied to gwr.predict()’s SDF too, where coefficients are suffixed _coef and the column literally named prediction is the prediction; predict() returned all NA.

  • Smaller: a logical response meets the same binary-response guard as 0/1; model_metrics() errors on a non-numeric response instead of returning n = 0; fitted.bayesian_fit() errors when the posterior cannot be drawn instead of returning silent NA; create_grid_polygons() refuses a grid above max_cells (default 1e6) up front; make_folds(method = "buffered_loo") states its guard in bytes (splits are ~4n² bytes; the old n = 20000 cap admitted 1.6 GB); -0 and 0 are the same coordinate in the duplicate-aware k-NN; .morans_i_for_k() returns the NA pair whenever the moments are unavailable.

  • Documented warnings are now R warnings. Eight paths the manual described as warning only wrote a logger line, invisible to tryCatch(warning = ), expect_warning() and options(warn = 2): residual_morans_i() returning NULL, the CRS assumption in ensure_projected() and stamping in harmonize_crs(), GWR collinearity, seed clamping in voronoi_seeds_kmeans() / get_voronoi_seeds(), dropped rows in ensure_stable_poly_id(), and the dropped column in assign_features_to_polygons(). Three deliberate methodological cautions (include_coords = TRUE, random_kfold feature selection, non-standardised Moran weights) stay logged and their documentation now says so.

  • predict() on a Bayesian GP fit depended on which other rows shared the call. brms 2.x stores Xgp, dmax and cmeans in a fit’s GP basis but not the Hilbert-space boundary L, so brms:::.data_gp() recomputes it from whatever rows predict() is handed. Every eigenfunction of the approximation therefore moved with the newdata bounding box while the fitted basis coefficients stayed put.
